reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: When completing a symmetric figure, the two halves must be ___.
Half of a shape is shown. The line of symmetry is vertical. To complete the shape, what do you do?
samples_reviewed.correct_answer: Draw the mirror image on the other side of the line.

samples_reviewed.question_text: A symmetric figure has a horizontal line of symmetry. If the top half has 3 squares, how many squares are in the bottom half?
A symmetric figure has a horizontal line of symmetry. If the top half has 3 squares, how many squares are in the bottom half?
Half of a shape is shown. The line of symmetry is vertical. To complete the shape, what do you do?
samples_reviewed.correct_answer: Draw the mirror image on the other side of the line.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency asks students to complete a symmetric figure; the samples test that completed halves must be mirror images, that completing across a vertical line means drawing the mirror image on the other side, and that a horizontal-line figure with 3 squares on top requires 3 on the bottom -- squarely on this node's 'complete a figure with respect to a line' task.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: 3 distinct question patterns appeared across the 5 sampled seeds (mirror-image definition, vertical-line completion instruction, horizontal-line square-count matching), a reasonable illustrative spread from the 2-axis/8-combo symmetry_slides registry rather than a single repeated stub.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Grade 3 Quarter 4's 22-word cap is comfortably met -- the longest sample, 'A symmetric figure has a horizontal line of symmetry. If the top half has 3 squares, how many squares are in the bottom half?', splits into two sentences of about 8 and 12 words.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The 8-combo symmetry_slides space, varying line orientation (vertical versus horizontal) and figure content (abstract mirror-image rule versus concrete square-counting), plausibly gives enough variety to build the figure-completion skill this competency targets.

competency_alignment.rationale: All three sample patterns are specifically about completing a figure around a stated line of symmetry, distinguishing this node from mat_g3_mg_q4_1's identification-only focus and mat_g3_mg_q4_0's slide/translation focus despite the shared DNA registry.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Content is discrete (small square counts, directional/mirror description), not a continuous numeric range, so scale appropriateness is a clean PASS for this figure-completion node.
